# Feature: Config and Storage Consolidation

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-041
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)

Make Yantra's installation surface production-ready before release: one storage root
instead of three, one schema-validated configuration file instead of four ad-hoc
parsers, complete CLI control over models/credentials/settings, and a first-class way
to open a run's results after it finishes.

A new user should be able to install Yantra, run `yantra init`, register a model, seed
an API key, and open their first brief — without ever hand-editing a YAML or JSON file,
and without wondering which of three directories holds their data.

### Problems this fixes (verified in the current tree)

| #   | Problem                                                                                                                                          | Evidence                                                                              |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P1  | Three storage roots on Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\yantra`, `%APPDATA%\yantra`, and `~/.config/yantra`                                              | `paths.ts:10` / `paths.ts:96`; three hardcoded sites below                            |
| P2  | **Live bug**: `ethics:` config, blocklist, and sanitizer host overrides read from a path nothing writes, so they are silently ignored on Windows | `ethics/config.ts:30`, `ethics/blocklist.ts:27`, `sanitizer/host-overrides.ts:72`     |
| P3  | `yantra config` is advertised but does not exist                                                                                                 | `init.ts:16`, `init.ts:166`                                                           |
| P4  | No CLI can **write** a keychain secret, yet three read paths depend on one                                                                       | `tavily.ts:49`, `brave.ts:51`, `--auth-secret` in `agent-options.ts:166`              |
| P5  | Registering a model means hand-editing Pi's `models.json` under the data dir                                                                     | `environment.ts:227`                                                                  |
| P6  | `config.yaml` has no schema; four call sites each parse and pluck their own sub-tree, so typos are silently ignored                              | `agent-options.ts:269`, `doctor.ts:318`, `search/config.ts:73`, `ethics/config.ts:31` |
| P7  | `retention.runsDays` is written by `init` and read by nothing; it is also the only camelCase key in a snake_case file                            | `init.ts:190`; no consumer in tree                                                    |
| P8  | Nine `YANTRA_AGENT_*` env vars exist undocumented as a set; search keys have no env path at all                                                  | `agent-options.ts:140-225`, `environment.ts:386`                                      |
| P9  | `--open` exists only on `ask` and `research`; there is no way to open a finished run's results after the fact                                    | `ask.ts:142`, `research.ts:149`                                                       |
| P10 | Corrupt-index backups accumulate unbounded (24 files since July on the author's machine)                                                         | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\yantra\index.db.corrupt.*`                                            |

### Out of scope

- **Upgrade/migration code.** Yantra is not released; this is a clean break. Nothing
  reads a legacy path, and no migration command ships. (`yantra config data-dir` in
  TASK-007 is a _user-invoked relocation_, a permanent feature, not migration.)
- Merging `yantra prefs` into `yantra config`. The two surfaces stay separate with
  explicit cross-redirects (see §2 Approach).
- Any change to run-artifact formats, workflow YAML, or the agent runtime itself.

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules are in `.spec-lite/memory.md`. Only additions and overrides appear here.

### Approach

**The organizing principle — two files, two questions.**

The root cause of the current confusion is that `config.yaml` and `profile.yaml` have no
stated division of labor, so settings landed in whichever file was convenient. This spec
fixes the boundary and then enforces it in the CLI:

| File                     | Answers                                                                                                                    | Owned by         | CLI                                              |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `~/.yantra/config.yaml`  | _What is installed and available?_ — storage paths, model registry, credential references, search providers, ethics policy | The installation | `yantra config`, `yantra model`, `yantra secret` |
| `~/.yantra/profile.yaml` | _What do I prefer?_ — which model, detail level, length, locale, sensitive-context grants                                  | The user         | `yantra prefs`                                   |

Neither command silently writes the wrong file. `yantra config set defaults.detail full`
fails with `that is a personalization key — use: yantra prefs set defaults.detail full`,
and the inverse redirect applies to `yantra prefs set` on a config-owned key. Redirects
are generated from the two schemas, so a key added to either file gets its redirect for
free.

**One root.**

`yantraHome()` resolves to `YANTRA_HOME` when set, else `join(homedir(), '.yantra')`, on
every platform. XDG support is removed — one rule, one documented layout. `dataDir()` and
`cacheDir()` are relocatable (§3), everything else is fixed under the home root.

**Typed configuration.**

A single `zod` schema (`packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`) replaces the four ad-hoc
parsers. The loader is `.strict()`: an unknown key is a validation error naming the key
and its nearest valid sibling, not a silent no-op. Load returns
`Result<YantraConfig, ConfigError>` per memory's error-handling rule — a malformed config
is an exit-1 validation failure with field context, never a silent reset to defaults.

**Deferred value references.**

Sensitive leaves hold a reference, not a value: `${env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}` or
`${secret:tavily.api_key}`. References are parsed and validated at load and resolved
**only at the execution boundary** — the same discipline the workflow `ValueRef` resolver
already uses (memory §Security). `yantra config get`/`list` print the reference text; no
command path can print a resolved secret.

**Models are Yantra-owned; Pi's file is derived.**

`yantra model add` writes a schema-validated entry to `config.yaml`'s `models:` block.
`<data>/pi/models.json` becomes a _projection_ generated from that block immediately
before `ModelRegistry.create()`. This keeps one source of truth and keeps the
third-party schema behind the adapter seam (memory §Architecture: provider SDK types stay
inside `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/`).

**One default, in the layer that already resolves it.**

The model registry records _what exists_; it has no `default` field. `yantra model default
<id>` writes `agent.provider` and `agent.model` into `profile.yaml`, which is exactly where
the existing `flag > env > profile > pinned default` chain (`diagnostics.ts:87`) already
looks. No new resolution logic is introduced, and there is no second place a default can
disagree with the first.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **`dataDir()` and `cacheDir()` keep a module-level memo.** Memory says avoid hidden
  singletons. These two functions are synchronous and called from ~15 sites across core;
  making them async to read `paths.data_dir` would force async contagion through the
  browser, index-db, scheduler, and extraction modules for no user-visible benefit. They
  therefore perform a memoized synchronous read of `config.yaml` on first call.

  Constraints that keep this honest, all test-enforced:
  - The memo is confined to `packages/core/src/config/resolved-paths.ts` and reachable
    only through `resetPathCache()` (exported for tests) and the two accessors.
  - The read is `readFileSync` of one small YAML, once per process.
  - Resolution is pure given `(env, file contents)`; the resolver function is exported
    separately from the memo and unit-tested with no I/O.
  - A parse failure falls back to the default location and emits one stderr warning; it
    never throws, because path resolution runs before the CLI's error handling exists.

- **No `Result` from `yantraHome()`/`configDir()`.** These are pure and total (env var or
  homedir), so they return `string`, matching the current signature.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

> No `.spec-lite/data_model.md` exists. This section defines the `config.yaml` schema,
> which is the feature's data model. No SQLite schema changes.

### Entity: `YantraConfig` — `~/.yantra/config.yaml`

```yaml
version: 1                          # literal 1; a future bump is a breaking-change gate

paths:
  data_dir: null                    # null → <home>/data
  cache_dir: null                   # null → <home>/cache

models:                             # the registry: what is available
  - id: claude-opus-4-7
    provider: anthropic
    api_key: ${env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}
    input: [text]
  - id: llama3.1:8b
    provider: ollama
    base_url: http://localhost:11434
    input: [text]

search:
  provider: auto
  fallback_chain: [tavily, brave, duckduckgo]
  tavily: { api_key: ${secret:tavily.api_key} }
  brave:  { api_key: ${secret:brave.api_key} }

ethics:
  robots_enabled: false
  user_agent: "YantraBot/0.1 (+https://yantra.dev)"
  rate_limit:
    default: { tokens_per_second: 1, burst: 2 }
    overrides: {}                   # host → { tokens_per_second, burst }

retention:
  runs_days: 30                     # renamed from runsDays; wired in TASK-004
  corrupt_index_keep: 3             # cap on index.db.corrupt.* backups

agent:
  pi_auth_path: null                # installation-level opt-in; NOT a preference
```

### Attributes

- **`paths`**:
  - `data_dir` (`string | null`) — absolute path; `null` means `<home>/data`. NOT NULL not
    applicable; validated as absolute when non-null.
  - `cache_dir` (`string | null`) — same contract.
- **`models[]`** (array, default `[]`):
  - `id` (`string`, min 1) — model identifier as the provider names it. UNIQUE within
    `(provider, id)`.
  - `provider` (`string`, min 1, lowercase-normalized) — `anthropic`, `ollama`, or custom.
  - `api_key` (`ConfigRef | null`, default `null`) — `${env:…}` or `${secret:…}` only; a
    literal key value is a **validation error** with a message pointing at `yantra secret set`.
  - `base_url` (`string | null`, default `null`) — required when `provider` is not a
    known hosted provider (e.g. `ollama`); enforced by a schema refinement.
  - `input` (`("text" | "image")[]`, default `["text"]`) — drives the existing
    `modelSupportsImageInput` probe (`environment.ts:129`), which currently fails closed
    on a registry miss.
- **`search.<provider>.api_key`** (`ConfigRef | null`) — same literal-value prohibition.
- **`ethics`** — mirrors today's `EthicsConfig` shape (`ethics/config.ts`), now typed.
- **`retention.runs_days`** (`int >= 0`, default 30) — `0` disables pruning.
- **`retention.corrupt_index_keep`** (`int >= 0`, default 3).

### `ConfigRef` value type

```
ConfigRef := "${env:"    ENV_NAME  "}"    where ENV_NAME  matches /^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$/
           | "${secret:" SECRET_KEY "}"   where SECRET_KEY matches /^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]*[a-z0-9])?$/
```

Parsed into `{ kind: 'env', name } | { kind: 'secret', key }` at load. A string that
contains `${` but does not match either form is a validation error naming the offending
path — never a silently-kept literal.

### Constraints

- `models[]` is UNIQUE on `(provider, id)`; a duplicate `yantra model add` is an error
  suggesting `--force` to overwrite.
- Unknown keys anywhere are rejected (`.strict()` at every object level).
- `paths.data_dir` and `paths.cache_dir` must be absolute and must not be nested inside
  each other or inside `~/.yantra/data` recursively (guards an obvious footgun).
- File mode `0o600` on write, matching today's `init` behavior (`init.ts:99`).

## 5. Dependencies

- **None new.** `zod`, `yaml`, `commander`, `pino`, and the keychain provider are all
  already in the tree. Comment-preserving writes use `yaml`'s existing Document API
  (`parseDocument`), not a new library.
- Existing capabilities relied on: `KeychainProvider` (`secrets/keychain.ts`),
  `LocalRunStore.listRuns()` (`workflow/replay/run-store.ts`), `openArtifact()`
  (`apps/cli/src/open-artifact.ts`), `profileSchema` (`profile/profile-file.ts`).

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: No authentication of Yantra itself. Provider and search credentials resolve
  through the keychain or `${env:}` references only at the execution boundary. `--auth-secret
<ref>` keeps its current runtime-key semantics (`agent-options.ts:166`) and now has a
  supported way to seed the referenced entry (TASK-008). File mode `0o600` on every config
  write.

- **Error Handling**: Follows the established exit-code contract — `1` validation (bad key,
  bad value, unknown run id, literal secret in config), `2` execution (relocation copy
  failure), `3` environment (keychain unavailable, unwritable storage root). Config load
  returns `Result` and never silently resets to defaults; the single exception is
  `resolveStorageDirs`, which must not throw because it runs before error handling exists
  and instead warns once on stderr. Every failure names one cause-specific next step, and
  two failures sharing a code must not read identically (memory §Coding Standards).

- **Logging**: Pino, structured, no secrets. Config values are logged as key paths only;
  `ConfigRef` values log as their reference text, never resolved. Canary-scan tests in
  TASK-005, TASK-008, and TASK-009 assert that no resolved credential reaches stdout,
  stderr, a log line, `models.json`, or a run artifact.

- **Security**: `yantra secret set` refuses argv input so credentials cannot enter shell
  history or `ps` output. A literal key in `config.yaml` is a validation error, not a
  warning. `redactConfigRefs` gates every render path. The Pi `models.json` projection
  carries references or omissions, never material.

- **Consistency**: `--json` on every new subcommand; `--print` (not `--stdout`/`--path`) as
  the non-launching sibling of `--open`, matching the negation-over-opt-in rule; `--force`
  spelled identically across `model rm`, `model add`, and `config data-dir`. New flags reuse
  existing spellings wherever a sibling command already names the same idea.
